> Hi Ananya — thanks for the heads up and for the sample request IDs.

Quick technical notes from triage (pre-bridge) — sending what I have so we’re prepared: 
- Observation: sustained increase in tail latency for sequences > 512 tokens originating from the checkout route. Concurrent small spike in internal 5xx (gateway-level) when autoscaler initiated a scale-down.
- Hypothesis: twofold — aggressive autoscaler policy combined with a KV cache eviction pattern for embeddings/KV that increased cold starts for some requests; system attempted to route traffic to a smaller pool and some replicas hit OOM/timeout before cold cache warmed.
- Immediate mitigations I’ll run if approved on the bridge: increase min-replicas on checkout pool by +2; temporarily relax autoscaler thresholds; enable short-lived cache warming on new replicas (preload top-10 prefixes).
- Owners: Dylan Brooks — run mitigations; Maya — coordinate customer agreement; Marissa — track customer comms and credit conversation.

I’ve attached triage snippets (logs + small grep outputs) for the three request IDs you provided. No PII in the snippets.

Dylan

Team — internal summary for leadership: 
- Impact: Saltbridge saw ~7% checkout failures for a 2 hour window (15:30–17:30 PDT 8/29), estimated lost checkout completions ~420.
- Root cause (working): autoscaler + cache-warmth timing leading to transient OOM/timeouts on scaled-down replicas.
- Actions taken: increased min-replicas on checkout pool (+2), relaxed autoscaler, deployed cache-prewarm on new replicas at 17:05 PDT. Customer routing to replica pool completed at 17:10. Error rate normalized by 17:28 PDT.
- Customer asks: formal RCA, timeline of fixes, and a commercial credit for the impacted window.

Request to finance/sales leadership (Jonas): approve up to a 20% one-off usage credit for the impacted billing window (HS record HS-12345). Marissa to finalize with customer after sign-off.

Subject: Saltbridge — Final RCA, completed mitigations, and owner cadence

Hi Ananya — thank you again for the bridge yesterday and for your patience while we completed the post-incident work. Below is the customer-facing RCA and the actions we’ve completed. We’ve attached the formal RCA PDF as well.

Summary (what happened):
- Between 15:30–17:30 PDT on 2028-08-29 Saltbridge experienced elevated checkout latency and a small 5xx spike (~7% of checkout requests).
- Cause: a race condition between autoscaler scale-down and cache warm-up on new replicas. When the pool contracted, some incoming real-time checkout requests hit replicas before the KV/embedding cache was populated; a subset of these requests encountered timeouts and 502/504 gateway errors as retries exceeded service timeouts.

Completed mitigations (done 8/29):
- Increased min-replicas on the checkout pool by +2 (Dylan) — completed 17:05 PDT.
- Relaxed autoscaler sensitivity for checkout route for 48 hours (Dylan) — completed 17:08 PDT.
- Deployed cache prewarm for the top-20 prefixes at new replica startup (Dylan) — completed 17:10 PDT.
- Temporary routing to warmed replica pool (Maya) — complete 17:10 PDT.

Planned longer-term fixes (commitments and owners):
- Autoscaler rule change: introduce a short cooldown window for scale-down that waits for cache-warm events (Owner: Dylan; ETA: 2028-09-07).
- Operational: add a check in our rollout runbook to validate cold-start metrics for new replicas (Owner: SRE runbook team; Owner point: jonas_weber; ETA: 2028-09-04).
- Monitoring: add a targeted alert for cold-start 95th/99th latency anomalies on critical routes (Owner: Dylan; ETA: 2028-09-01).

Commercial remediation: Marissa has proposed a one-off 18% usage credit for the impacted window; pending finance approval (HS-12345). Marissa will finalize with Saltbridge by 8/31 EOD.

Attachments: saltbridge-rca-final.pdf (pdf) — includes timeline, graphs, and request ID correlation. Also: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1X_saltbridge-rca for live doc.

Please reply if you need any additional detail. Would you like a short postmortem call next week to walk this through with your ops team?

Best,
Maya Srinivasan
